text.title: Laravel Umbrella Core Rules
text.summary: 9 testable rules grounding the Laravel umbrella methodology — 5 operating rules for how the app runs, then 4 framework fundamentals for how it is written. Each rule pairs a binary check + sourced rationale.

rule.statement: For every feature, the agent MUST route to the relevant sub-methodology: HTTP layering → `php-laravel-patterns`; ORM details → `php-eloquent`; queue work → `php-laravel-queues`; tests → `php-phpunit-testing`. Generic Laravel advice MUST NOT replace the sub-methodology's rules.
rule.rationale: Umbrella methodologies must dispatch; pretending to cover everything in one file misses the testable detail per sub-area.

rule.statement: `composer.json` MUST require PHP `^8.2`. Laravel `^10.0` minimum (`^11.0` preferred). Targeting PHP < 8.2 or Laravel < 10 is forbidden in new code.
rule.rationale: Readonly properties, enums, `Attribute::make` and current security patches require PHP 8.1+ / Laravel 10+; older targets miss critical fixes.

rule.statement: Production environments MUST set `QUEUE_CONNECTION` to a real driver (`redis` / `database` / `sqs`). `sync` is forbidden in any `*-prod`, `*-staging` env.
rule.rationale: `sync` executes inline, blocking the request and silently inverting the latency contract.

rule.statement: `.env` MUST live outside VCS. Code MUST read secrets via `config('service.key')` (a `config/*.php` file is the only place `env()` may be called) — direct `env()` calls inside services, controllers or providers are forbidden because `config:cache` freezes empty values. Deploy MUST run `php artisan config:cache` and `route:cache`.
rule.rationale: `env()` inside services returns null after `config:cache` runs in production deploy; the caches are also where the per-request bootstrap cost is bought back.

rule.statement: `php artisan schedule:work` and `php artisan queue:work` MUST run under Supervisor (or systemd) with auto-restart on failure. Cron-based `schedule:run` MUST be the single entry every minute (never duplicated per task).
rule.rationale: Crashed workers without supervisor silently stop processing; per-task cron entries multiply concurrency and break locks.

section.title: Framework fundamentals
section.p: The rules above constrain how a Laravel app runs; these four constrain how it is written. Laravel offers several ways to do the same thing — facades, helpers, container, providers, contracts — and only one of each pair survives `route:cache`, `config:cache` and a unit test that never boots the framework.

rule.statement: Every contract (interface) MUST be bound to an implementation in a Service Provider's `register()` method, and the provider registered in `config/app.php` (or `bootstrap/providers.php` on Laravel 11). Inline `app()->bind(...)` in a controller, service or middleware is forbidden.

rationale.source: Laravel reference — service container + service providers

rule.rationale: Providers are loaded once at boot; an inline bind only exists after the code path that ran it, so the first request after deploy fails.

rule.statement: Service classes MUST constructor-inject contracts (`__construct(private MailService $mail)`). Facades (`Mail::send`, `Cache::get`) are permitted only in controllers, middleware and artisan commands.
rule.rationale: Facades resolve from the container at call time, so replacing them in a test needs `Mail::fake()` boilerplate; constructor injection is mockable with plain PHPUnit and needs no framework boot.

rule.statement: Routes MUST be declared in `routes/*.php` and MUST point at a controller method (`Route::get('/', [HomeController::class, 'index'])`). Route closures and route definitions inside controllers, providers or middleware are forbidden.
rule.rationale: `php artisan route:cache` serialises the route table and fails outright on a closure; inline routes are also invisible to `route:list` and to observability tooling.

rule.statement: Cross-cutting concerns — auth checks, CORS, rate limiting, locale, tenancy — MUST be implemented as middleware and attached to a route group. Repeating the same check in N controllers is forbidden.
rule.rationale: Middleware is the framework's own seam for the concern; controller-level repetition drifts the moment one of the N copies is updated.
